title: Pyramid hierarchy of computer storage
summary: The storage pyramid compares speed, capacity, cost per unit capacity, and persistence across storage levels.
context: The pyramid widens from top to bottom across five levels. The top three levels sit inside a green box labeled CPU and are grouped on the left as "Cache"; the fourth level is labeled "Memory", and the fifth level is labeled "Disk".

frames.title: Pyramid hierarchy of computer storage
frames.explanation: On the right, the upward arrow is labeled "Speed, Cost": higher levels provide faster access at higher cost per unit capacity. The downward arrow is labeled "Capacity, Persistence": lower levels offer larger capacity, and HDD/SSD at the bottom retains data long term without power. Cache and memory are volatile storage and lose data when power is removed.

tables.caption: Five storage levels from top to bottom
